content.text:
Here are the sections you want, Cael:

---

**🤖 AI Drone Swarms — Emil Michael's key quotes:**

> "I believe that a sophisticated drone war is going to be drone swarms controlled by AI to some degree or another. To what degree the control matters... the Ukrainians and Russians do something called a kill box where they lose comms because it's jammed and then it just starts going in a box and looking for the person they're trying to get — they're starting to use AI to do that."

> "China has this ability already probably times some magnitude. They have drone swarms because they can force the companies that make them to interoperate. Heterogeneous autonomy — taking different kinds of drones and making sure they're not going after the same target — is a pretty complex thing they're definitely working on."

**On AI autonomy limits today:**

> "We're just at the very beginning of this stuff. We wouldn't feel that a system would have sort of real risk for a civilian is ready to launch yet. We're just trying to get basic autonomy in drones, basic autonomy in underwater unmanned vehicles..."

**Golden Dome — the compelling full-autonomy case:**

> "A Chinese hypersonic missile comes up. You've got 90 seconds before it separates and all kinds of decoys. A human can't have the reaction time, doesn't have the ability to discriminate. That's a pretty low-risk thing because it's in space and you're just trying to hit something that's trying to hit you."

---

**🔥 Anthropic/Pentagon Fallout — the core issue:**

The breakdown wasn't really about murderbots or mass surveillance (the PR framing). Emil's actual concerns:

1. **Reliability risk** — Anthropic held the control plane for the model in AWS GovCloud and could change model weights at any time. One Anthropic exec called Palanteer *after* the Maduro raid to ask if their software was used — implying they might pull the license if it was.

2. **Terms of service as a kill switch** — Emil: *"What if this software went down, some guard rail kicked up, some refusal happened for the next fight and we left our people at risk?"*

3. **The "call me" problem** — Dario reportedly said "just call me if you need another exception." Emil's response: *"What if the balloon's going up at that moment? I'm not going to call you."*

4. **Their constitution ≠ US Constitution** — Emil: *"Anthropic has its own constitution, its own soul. It's not the US Constitution. So you're subject to that plus whatever whims and how that changes."*

---

**🔗 Your "Identity as Immune System" angle:**

This is a perfect real-world case study. The core security failure Emil describes is **identity and authorization at the model layer** — a private company's internal policy acting as an override on a sovereign military's operational decisions. The DoD couldn't trust the model's behavior because they didn't own its identity or governance layer.

That's exactly the gap Conductor is designed to close: pre-auth architecture where behavioral policy is owned by the deploying organization, not the model vendor. Emil basically described the threat model for your research out loud on a podcast.
